newsitem.title: USA: US House sets Feb 27 for Fed chairman's testimony.
newsitem.headline: US House sets Feb 27 for Fed chairman's testimony.

text.p: The House Banking Committee has tentatively set the Federal Reserve chairman's semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony for Feb. 27, a committee spokesman said Monday.
The Senate Banking Committee, which will hear the testimony first, has not yet set a date, a committee spokesman said.
The Federal Reserve chairman reports to Congress twice a year in Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on the outlook for the economy. The House and Senate alternate which side holds the hearing first.
By law the Fed is required to "transmit" the Humphrey-Hawkins report to Congress not later than Feb. 20 and July 20 of each year, a congressional aide said.
"The law does not require Congress to have a hearing on a certain date," although the banking committees try to hold the hearings as close to those dates as possible, he said.
The Senate is scheduled to be in recess for the Presidents' Day holiday Feb. 14-23.
